newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu accuses Arafat of breaking promises.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu accuses Arafat of breaking promises.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of breaking a promise to rein in militants after a double suicide bombing killed 13 people in Jerusalem on Wednesday.

"We expect the Palestinian Authority and its leader to begin to fight terror as they are committed to, as they haven't done until today, that they will take all the steps required against these terrorists and their operators who roam free," he told a news conference after visiting some of the wounded in hospital.
"They must be jailed, their weapons and their explosives collected," said Netanyahu, elected prime minister 14 months ago on a promise to bolster Israelis' security.
Israel sealed off the Palestinians of the West Bank and Gaza Strip and Netanyahu called an emergency security cabinet meeting for 6 p.m. (1500 GMT) to discuss further Israeli steps.
Netanyahu said 150 leaders of the Moslem militant groups Hamas and Islamic Jihad in Palestinian self-rule areas had in the past been set free by "like savage animals to prowl in our streets".
"We aren't ready to accept that murderous acts will be part of our daily lives every few weeks and months and we will await suitable steps," he said.
Israeli police said 13 people, including the two suicide bombers, died in the attack on the Jewish street market in Jerusalem. They said 157 people were wounded.
Arafat called Netanyahu to express his condolences but Netanyahu said: "We expect not only words of condolences but also words of condemnation."
"We expect real action, have the right to demand real action. And we cannot be satisfied only with deeds. We also want to see words, hear other words. Other acts and other words.

"That is to say not words of condolence after murder has been committed but words of condemnation, words of education to the Palestinian population, words that say terror and violence are not acceptable. Not words that call for the continuation of the struggle by all means possible against the Zionist occupier...

"If we're heading toward peace we're going to peace in all ways: in words, deeds, policy, not one-off, not for one minute, by way of lip service, but continuous action that brings about a change of 180 degrees from what we've seen in the last weeks and months. That's what we expect to see. It's our right to see this change," Netanyahu told reporters.
